module: Carry out and maintain the assessment

lesson.title: Case: choose and defend the assessment route
lesson.summary: Defend the procedure using the actual case conditions.

prerequisites.reason: The HR case requires the provider internal-control procedure.
The biometric case requires the standards-dependent assessment branch.
The case requires evidence and access decisions under an external assessment.
The case includes a change after the initial assessment.

blocks: **Three route decisions:** Northbridge has the stipulated Annex III employment use. Beacon has a lawful point 1 biometric use and only partial application of the relevant standard. Harbour has the stipulated Section A medical product with sector-required third-party assessment. Assume a supported temporal interpretation for these exercises; actual release dates still need F03's check.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 43–45; Annexes VI and VII; CRA Article 12(2)–(3)

blocks: Northbridge follows Annex VI internal control; its provider verifies quality management, technical compliance and actual consistency. Beacon follows Annex VII because partial standard application triggers that procedure. Harbour follows the required sector procedure with incorporated AI requirements. Their common high-risk label does not make their procedures identical.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 43–45; Annexes VI and VII; CRA Article 12(2)–(3)

blocks: A proposed unplanned change affects an assessed system's compliance. Review whether it is substantial and apply reassessment even for continued use. Under Annex VII, involve the body in deciding new assessment versus supplement. Check the old certificate's conditions rather than assuming it covers the changed release.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 43–45; Annexes VI and VII; CRA Article 12(2)–(3)

blocks: A separate digital product claims CRA evidence allows any assessment route. Check CRA scope, deemed cybersecurity conditions and the distinct Article 12(2)–(3) interactions, especially important/critical products. The medical case's stipulated exclusion is not a CRA exemption for every other digital product.
